Customer leaning toward hybrid: hosted for early tests, dedicated/private for PII-sensitive pipelines. Security and SLA questions were high priority.

Context window sizing and cost/latency impact
Tool-calling / function calling for structured outputs
Hosting modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-30 17:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Oliver Park (Kilnware CTO), Sana Patel (Kilnware ML Lead), Jamal Rivers (Kilnware DevOps), Lina Gomez (Kilnware PM)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, joined by Diego our SE and Priya from solutions, quick roll call?
00:12 Oliver: Oliver here, Sana, Jamal and Lina on our side. Thanks, Maya.
00:18 Maya: Awesome, goal for today is to understand your workloads, model/latency/cost constraints, and what you need for tool-calling and privacy so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Sana, do you want to kick off with the use cases?
00:30 Sana: Sure, yeah. We're building a knowledge assistant over our client contracts and internal runbooks, plus a code helper for platform engineers. Need strong context for long docs — some contracts are 60–80k tokens, so we're thinking 100k context for a subset. Multilingual support matters, we have documents in EN, FR, ES, and Japanese occasionally. Latency targets: sub-2s for single-turn search-summary outputs, but for long form generation we can tolerate 3–6s. Cost is also a big driver, we can't blow up runway, so we need to see unit economics.
01:05 Diego: Got it, so two distinct patterns: search/summary with low-latency SLO, and long-context synthesis where throughput matters. Quick question on the 100k requirement — is that maximum or sporadic?
01:16 Sana: Sporadic, maybe 5–10% of calls. Most interactions are within 8–32k. But when legal review needs the whole doc, we need the full window, otherwise we'd fallback to chunking.
01:27 Lina: Also note data residency for EU customers, and some contracts contain PII; Jamal can talk about isolation.
01:34 Jamal: We're constrained by security — SOC2 is standard, but some enterprise partners require dedicated VPC and customer-managed KMS, and we have air-gapped prospects for later.
01:44 Maya: Totally understood. On models, are you leaning open-source models or considering closed models?
01:48 Oliver: Open preferred for cost and control. We evaluate Llama-3-ish family, Mistral, and MPT-type kernels. Curious how Redwood handles different quantization/latency profiles and the tradeoffs for 32k vs 100k.
02:02 Diego: Practically, for 100k you need a model with efficient attention kernels and memory footprint optimizations. For example, we see Llama-3-34B quantized variants hitting the 100k feasibly with higher mem, or newer sparse attention variants; Mistral-7B excels on cost for shorter contexts but struggles at 100k without chunking. We can run benchmarks with your prompt distribution.
02:28 Sana: When you say "run benchmarks" — what do you measure? Throughput, p99 latency, cost per 1k tok?
02:34 Diego: We'll measure median and p95 latency for both cold and warmed KV-cache, tokens per second throughput, and a cost model normalized to your request mix (we'll show hosted vs dedicated unit costs). We'll include function-calling latency overhead and streaming vs non-streaming differences.
02:50 Maya: Important to mention tool-calling — do you expect external tool invocations (API calls, DB lookups) to be orchestrated by Redwood or by you?
02:58 Lina: We want Redwood to handle function-call style outputs (structured JSON responses) and ideally provide a way to call our internal search service with a signed short-lived token, but orchestration stays with us.
03:10 Diego: That's straightforward — Redwood supports structured function calling and tool invocation hooks; for hosted we provide signed webhook patterns, for Dedicated/Private you can peer and put the tool endpoints inside a VPC for lower trust surface. There are variants where Redwood will call your endpoint with mTLS if you want.
03:28 Jamal: On peering — what's the network setup for Private? We need to know egress IPs and if we can do VPC peering, or if you support private connectors.
03:38 Maya: For Private we provide customer-managed control plane and on-prem options, VPC peering is supported, and you'll get static egress IP ranges for allowlisting. We'll include network appendix in the security packet.
03:50 Oliver: Good. Also curious about model version pinning and rollouts — we want reproducibility across experiments.
03:56 Diego: You can pin model versions, roll out canary variants, and we support automatic fallback to smaller or quantized variants on capacity constraints. The console shows token-level diffs so you can track regressions.
04:08 Sana: Great. A few performance specific questions: 32k vs 100k context will change memory behavior and batching — how does Redwood handle batching when some requests are 100k?
04:20 Diego: We do workload-aware batching: requests are bucketed by sequence-length distribution; large-context requests can be routed to dedicated lanes that avoid blocking low-latency short requests. For Dedicated you can reserve a pool for long-context so you don't impact p95 on short queries. That isolation comes with a cost but keeps SLOs.
04:39 Lina: Any quick numbers—like relative cost delta between 32k and 100k for token generation with Llama-3-34b?
04:47 Diego: Ballpark: 100k active KV will increase memory and kernel time; raw token compute might be ~2.5x–4x depending on sparsity and quantization. We'll produce concrete numbers once we benchmark with your payloads.
04:59 Oliver: Ok. On multilingual: our main concern is document fidelity in French and Japanese — do you have curated model recommendations?
05:07 Diego: Mistral-family and certain Llama-3 variants have strong multilingual baselines, but for Japanese we often recommend models with explicit Japanese pretraining or instruction-tuned adapters; we can test your dev set. Also note that model size doesn't always predict multilingual quality — evals are necessary.
05:23 Sana: We'll share a small eval corpus — maybe 200 doc pairs across EN/FR/JP — and you'd run BLEU/ROUGE-ish and human spot checks?
05:31 Diego: Yes, we'll run automated metrics and sample-blind human evals, and include hallucination/regression checks. We'll surface quality vs latency tradeoffs in the spreadsheet.
05:40 Maya: Any compliance flags or red lines from your side?
05:44 Jamal: KMS integration is mandatory for production, and SSO via SAML, RBAC for team roles, and audit logs for every tokenized request ideally — at minimum for export. Also retention policies: some customers require zero retention.
05:58 Priya: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys for enterprise. Audit logs are available; retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private. We'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
06:12 Oliver: About pilot: we want to try hosted first to get faster time-to-value, then move to Dedicated for the PII pipelines. What's a typical pilot flow?
06:20 Maya: Pilot usually is 2–4 weeks: small seat in Hosted, bench with your payloads, then a scoped Dedicated pilot if you need VPC/KMS. We can provide a pricing credit for pilot measurement.
06:31 Lina: Pricing question: flat monthly vs usage? For Dedicated is it reserved capacity?
06:36 Maya: Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit tiers and predictable throughput pricing; we can model both.
06:43 Oliver: Competitors — we've looked at PineCloud and Infralytix, they have nicer integrated tool GUIs but their latency was worse in our tests. How do you compare?
06:54 Diego: We focus on runtime performance and predictable SLOs — our routing and KV cache strategies often give better p95 in production. We'll include a benchmark that mirrors your observed traffic.
07:05 Sana: A few clarifying points: when you say KV cache warm state, do we need to do anything to warm it?
07:11 Diego: You can pre-warm by replaying recent sessions or via an API to pin prefixes; Redwood also has automatic prefix caching heuristics. For contractual guarantees we quantify cold vs warm p95 separately.
07:24 Jamal: For compliance we'll want a contractual clause around data deletion for Hosted pilot — can you accommodate?
07:30 Maya: Yes, for pilot we can set a retention window and a deletion SLA. We'll put that in the security packet.
07:38 Oliver: Ok let's talk next steps.
07:41 Maya: Diego will run the benchmarks on your sample set (32k and 100k runs) and return a spreadsheet, I'll send pricing and the security packet, and Jamal will share network constraints. We'll aim to reconvene after results — sounds like 1 week?
07:55 Lina: One week is fine.
07:58 Maya: Quick recap: pilot on Hosted, benchmarks for model candidates (Llama-3-34B variants, Mistral-7B, MPT-30B-ish), multilingual eval, function/tool-calling checks, and security docs. Anything else?
08:13 Oliver: Maybe one more ask — can you include an example of function-calling latency (end-to-end with an external DB lookup)?
08:19 Diego: Yes, we'll include a simulated function-call in the benchmark to measure added latency and failure handling.
08:25 Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.
08:30 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: some product names maybe mis-stated, e.g., "KV cach" or "smal" for SAML; occasional speaker overlap.
